comment: Definitely take the adventure trail
Avoid weekends after 9am, extremely crowded with non-hikers

The main trail up to the view points were very crowded. Once we passed the major lookouts, the trail clear up a bunch. The main trail and loop were moderate in difficulty. However, the Adventure Trail option was a lot more challenging than I expected. It included crawling through caves and down pretty high drops, so be ready for that. The bugs weren’t bad since it was so windy at the top. Since it was pretty busy, parking was a bit of a nightmare. I would recommend getting there early.
Not much parking availability after the morning so come as early as possible

Nice trail, no bugs, wear your appropriate shoes, can be slippery on the rocks. I would not recommend with really young kids. Bring water
Amazing views (many cliffs)
Lots of great cliff views, bring lots of water of you are doing the 8k loop, sunglasses not needed nice and shady.
Super fun hike! We did it with some running and it was awesome! Love it. No bugs, dry ground, and well maintained signages.
south loop has some overgrown trees/bushes
Longer than expected but excellent hike with incredible views.
Great views, but got to be careful with kids getting too close to the cliff. Nice trail with lots of shades. Great marks along the trail
If you're doing the blue trail, I'd suggest skipping the forest walk - follow the red blazes until you get to the lookout, then follow the blue blazes as long as you want before turning back.
Beautiful trail with great views. Quieter in the morning.
It was my first time hiking, and I had so much fun, I can definitely see myself doing more and more hikes in the future!
Beautiful views,  some steep climbs, lots of birds, well maintained.
Trail in pretty good condition. It poured while I was hiking but it did not get too muddy.
Amazing trail for fall colors, a bit muddy and slippery after the rain but stunning and so peaceful

Absolutely amazing hike!! We followed the red trail to begin, took the yellow adventure trail (so much fun, but not suitable for everyone, especially pets!), then followed the blue trail all the way around in a counter clockwise direction. The views were stunning, lots of challenging sections with steep stairs and some ladders (adventure trail), and incredible rock formations. Plenty of view points once you reach the top section!! The trail markers were sparse in some areas and conflicted with the map at the trail head so do download the map if you can.
Really nice trail with beautiful views! Some rocks are slippery so make sure to wear good footwear.  We went on a weekday in October and it was very quiet. It took us about 3 hours.

i am visiting the area on a long weekend, and so had to share the trail with a robust holiday crowd. (plus the weather was stunning). but i went into the further reaches and had some quiet  stretches and had  the trail mostly to myself. 
it is beautiful, and in parts, spectacular. took me three hours total, but i am often stopping to identify plants and just take in the beauty.
Beautiful views!!
It took us 5 hours to do the loop

Lovely walk through a boulder-strewn forest with incredible cliffside views. Fairly easy, but a few rocky bits that can be slippery, particularly if you come on a rainy day like we did. Big parking lot, so looks like it can get busy, but well worth it.
Must see trail, make time for the whole thing. You will likely linger at spots. Good for photography.

Beautiful day September 8. The trail is fairly easy to follow. There is the odd spot where it’s hard to know which way to go. I saw a lot of people with dogs but there is a section that is like a ladder which could be very tricky with a dog. I found using a walking stick very helpful when coming back down. It is rocky but manageable. I so enjoyed eating lunch at the top. There are some steep sections.

Beautiful views across forest and lakes in the distance. We did the short plus longer loop. The longer loop continues along the bluff affording many more view points.  The other section was an easy path through pleasant woods. Trail has some slippery ricks with moss and some steps up and down- recommend hiking boots and a hiking stick, though most other hikers were wearing tennis shoes so certainly you can.
Amazing views. Left at 8 and had the blue trail to ourselves. Crowded parking lot on return.

We did it on Labour Day weekend so it was very busy (at least on the 5km trail). We did the long trail, took just over 2 hours with lots of short water breaks (we took our dog) and photo stops. Very easy trail, some rocky areas, one tighter squeeze by the steep stairs. Overall very nice walk.
Nice walk through forested area, some climbing and lots of great lookouts over the Georgian bay

Amazing trail with great views. We started on the red trail, then continued on blue to do the longer hike along the ridge. The views along the ridge are spectacular and well worth it. The route back goes through a pretty deciduous forest
Trail is very well marked and very busy. Amazing views! The last turn toward the parking lot needs to be better marked.
Very nice.  The long trail is nice.
My trek was overall good-moderately challenging if you stick to the red trail, but a bit tougher if you take the blue path. The views from the top were definitely worth it.

The trail was very nice with a good mix of easy and technical terrain.  Lots of great lookout points along the trail.  
Only downside was the gross overflowing porta potties.  Please clean them.

If doing this loop counter-clockwise, there is only one slightly confusing trail junction. Otherwise, trial is super well marked and easy to follow, with several great lookout spots towards the end of the trail. In general it is very flat, only a few obstacles and little inclines. Should be rated easy.
Some big stone steps.
Easy trail with a nice lookout. Dog friendly.
Hard to get to.

Come EARLY on the weekends for parking. We got here at 9AM on a July Saturday morning and it was empty. By the time we finished (12:30) both lots were FULL. Parking is a minimum $13 donation to keep the trail running. You pay online when you get here. WORTH IT. IT'S BEAUTIFUL. I do not recommend small kids!! And wear closed toed shoes with a solid ankle base: lots of rocky spots! Fit, athletic dogs will be able to do the course, including the latter.
Lots of other lookouts along the back half of the trail

Abit of overgrowth on the trails and lots poison ivy around the look out areas, I would advise wearing pants. Some stunning views on the lookout points. Trail was fairly dry but would advise wearing proper footwear.
Nice trail. We did this with our 6.5 year old so took close to 4 hours with breaks and the adventure trail.
Great view at the top, the extra 5 km loop is a bit of work on a hot summer day, but well worth it.
Wonderful trail was spectacular views. Would’ve been even better on a sunny clear day.

Took the loop clockwise to get to the views first.  Also took the adventure side trail:  challenging but fairly short.  Good boots a must.  Lost the trail briefly and thought I had to crowl through a hole in the rock haha.  After the climb along the loop it’s mostly easy and flat and not a lot of people.

This hike is a staple for manitoulin island for a reason there’s a bit of something for everyone. The trail is easy to intermediate with more difficult sections but mostly easy. Great for most people!
Well marked. Exciting. Good views. Can be dangerous. Concerning cracks out of no where.
Some steep sections.

Trail is well marked and maintained. Not much traffic once you start the loop and leave the main lookout trail. Not super challenging. Mostly flat after the initial climb to the ridge line then downhill back to the parking lot.
Marked out well! Incline is fairly easy, great views along the way. Would recommend doing loop in counter clockwise so you end with the views!
It was really nice, we did the adventure trail and it was a bit intense but super fun!
Beautiful, well marked trail! Would recommend.

First little bit of the trail is a little challenging, otherwise it's all flat. Very rewarding hike - views along the cliffs are amazing (only see this when you do the full trail). Highly recommend going when leaves are fully changed.
The first couple km’s have the most steep areas, the rest is relatively flat just watch your footing. Well marked. Great trail would do it again!

Gorgeous views with very minimal effort required - lots of people with dogs on the trail. The 500m adventure trail is quite fun for anyone wanting a bit of an extra challenge, but probably nothing that  older kids can't handle. Freshly fallen tree obstructing the trail ~7km in, easy to cross but also easy to lose the trail lol.

Great trail. Climbing up rocks, some stairs, some flat through the woods . Beautiful are through the woods. The views from lookouts were stunning . Colours  were pretty with leaves turning red but still lots of maples green leaves.
Well marked trails. Loved the long loop. Some steep inclines to get to the top but flat for the most part.
AGH MY PHONE IS GONNA DIE SO I CANT CONTINUE BUT I DID THE LOOP WND ITS AWESOME
Very flat....except for a short steep climb with ropes.  Views of the valley are gorgeous
Good conditions. Marked well. Beat traffic by going early
Nice and easy trail with scenic lookouts!
To clean the bathrooms, so disgusting cannot even use them
We completed the main and southloop trail (approx 9km). We enjoyed the lookouts

Incredible views from the escarpment. I hiked in the reverse direction of the loop on AllTrails, taking in the views first and then enjoying an easy, pleasant walk through the forest on the way back to the trailhead.
Perfect conditions right now and as always epic views. The trail is easily followed and well marked. The best time to go in my opinion is early in the morning, beat the crowds and the summer heat.
Beautiful hike with countless scenic views. Check out the Adventure Trail for increased difficulty and fun. Enjoyed some extra ladders, steep staircases, rope climbs, and caves. We had a blast.
Conditions are good a couple rough patches but easily manageable. The views along the ridge just keep getting better it seems every 20ft there’s another one.
Great trail. Full of ups and downs. Kept as much original to the area.
So fun you can do a couple of different loops to extend the hike and get all the trails
K

Great views! So pretty!  Found it difficult at times to see the trail signs though. Might be beneficial to have signs to mark the closed trails. Also marked distances to trail head and look out point. Trail in decent shape despite recent rains.  Definitely took us longer than the 2 1/2 hours

A moderate trail with lots of rocks & roots & a steep ladder. Nice & forested. Proper hiking foot wear is strongly recommended. Tranquility of the forest was spoiled by traffic noise & the noise from quarry machines at a couple of viewpoints. Have hiked better trails.

Absolutely gorgeous trail. Do yourself a favour and hit the full loop. If you hike the cliff edge first you are treated to a lovely walk in the woods for the remainder surrounded by huge varieties of mushrooms and butterflies.
Awesome trail! Worth starting it early in the morning to avoid the crowds. Amazing views.
At about 3kms in trail diverts. From old trail to new one.
awesome views.  all trails failed a few times on me
Loved it
Beautiful views, really fun trail. Adventure Trail was great, highly recommend!

Parking lot empty when we arrived at 8:20a.  Trail well marked on trees (in the fall) but underbrush high: suspect summer leaves obscure the markers…

‘Adventure’ side trail with rickety appearing, though solid ladders.  Pretty views - though graffiti distracted.  Would not want to use trail if ground wet.

It was beautiful. It will most likely be beautiful in a few weeks with all the fall colours too. Red trail was rocky and rooted though well marked, many look off points. The transition from red to blue after the saucer lookoff was overgrown and we didn't realize the trail was on the rocks. The blue trail is not well or consistently marked. There are lots of mushrooms
Great trail! As said before hiking shoes are a good idea. We'll marked, take your time with rock covered sections.

This medium to difficult trail is VERY WELL MARKED.   Previous reviews seem to be from a few years ago. The blazes are obvious and signs point to the parking lot upon your return so you don’t turn the wrong ( long) way. The Red Trail forms a loop that takes a couple hours of steady hiking. The Blue Trail adds a further 5 km and we chose to skip it. Do not go later than 10 am if you want nature to yourself. Do wear proper footwear and clothing. This is not an open toed shoe affair. Do not bring unleashed dogs. The Lookout is breath taking and well worth the climb.
Level of difficulty is moderate. Beautiful lookouts.
Easy hike, if your a rock climber bring 70m rope and a double rack of trad gear =D
Really nice hike with nice views. MUST do the adventure portion of the hike
Trail quite hard to follow. Very easy and very flat though aside from a small portion at beginning/end.
Great trail. Start early to avoid crowds.

almost no bugs today!!! a few horse/deer flys between 6 and 9 am

First part of the blue trail poorly marked from the lookouts to the 9 km loop. must use the alltrails app and gpsggggggg
Use the map. Trail not well marked in areas

The reviews so far are accurate. We started the hike at about 10am and it was very quiet then. By the time we were going back down 2hours later, we crossed a lot of people making their way up. We met absolutely no one on the blue trail. I did get a few scratches from the tree branches but it was worth it. The view at the top is fantastic. Note that there is steep ladder (about 4 meters i would say) to climb early on in the hike, and I do not know whether dogs or people with some mobility issues could do it. Outside if that, it is a very pleasant hike!

Great trail with amazing views! Easy to follow, ample free parking. But it did get super busy in the afternoon, which I’m not crazy about. The Adventure Trail was very cool, and a little challenging with my dog even though he is no stranger to challenging trails. The ladder rungs are just a little further apart than he’s used to.
Such a beauty trail. Lots of views and vantage points

Wear pants. The blue trail is not as well traveled as the red, so in spots, it's super narrow with scratchy vegetation. Ask me how I know! 

The red trail is fine in good walking shoes, but the blue trail is more rough and I wished for proper hiking boots before I was done.

Great hike, worth the scratches and bruises

Parking lots gets filled up quickly on a weekend and so does the pathway. I opted for the full loop and not a lot of people on that side of the trail. The rocky terrain and adventure parts of the trail can be moderately challenging. Great views all along the cliff side. There’s also washrooms ( Porta Potty )available in the parking lot. Overall, a great place to experience and worth the drive out. Happy Hiking !

I started the trail at 11am, there were people but the climb up wasn’t that busy. I recommend hiking boots or shoes as there are a lot of rocks. Took the red trail the way up and the blue trail the way back. I recommend taking the blue trail on the way back; amazing hidden plateaus to sit, take in the view and for photos. Using the trails map will help you with the first half of the blue trail as it is not obviously marked.
Great trail and rewarding view at the top. Strongly recommend taking an adventure spur
Excellent trail conditions with lots of beautiful lookouts.  Was quiet in the morning but got pretty busy in the afternoon.
The trail along the bluff is beautiful, adventure side trail is fun, the blue trail inside the forest has not much to offer, should have gone the same way.
Middle of November trail conditions still excellent, amazing views from the lookouts

I can see the first half potentially being a challenge for young children or small dogs but I did see a few on the trail. I came at 10:30 on a Tuesday morning and ran into a few people but it wasn’t as busy as I expected based on other reviews. Highly recommend to anyone, the views are beautiful!

Great hike! The short section of the trail was very busy but the longer loop was nice and quiet. Really exceptional views and lots of look outs to take them all in. 

Fee payment instructions are found on the instruction board near the parking lot.

The adventure trail was AWESOME! Loved exploring, rock scrambling, crawling through some little caves, the thin wooden ladders, etc! There is an alternate path if this isn't so much your thing :) the views from the ridge were beautiful, loved seeing more of the escarpment and watching the birds of prey circling nearby!
Great mix of terrains! Totally worth doing the full loop!
Good trail, up to the lookout was busy but only ran into a couple others on the big loop (blue)
Very nice hike. Adventure trail is hard and really nice. Loop is a bit longer then expected. It’s more 10km then 9km. Multiple lookout were fantastique. Loop on our way back is smooth. Worth it.

The Adventure Trail is a must!!! So unique! Watch out for poison ivy if you do the loop. There’s a lot just past the lookout if you’re coming on to the loop from that end. Stay on the path and look where you’re walking, and you should be fine.
It's a really great hike. Conditions were perfect. Adventure trail is a must.
Best trail ever! Please make sure to bring back your garbage
Nice. Much easier than other reports suggest. Adventure trail was fun. Went early in the day and very busy by the time we were done.

Great loop trail. Passable for our medium/large active dog - only one set of stairs. Ladders not suitable for dogs are on ‘adventure’ section of trail. Very quiet on the loop as well but busy on the initial trail to the lookout. Lots of great lookouts. Definitely recommend!

Great trail - only one set of stairs. Passable for our dog (medium to large size active dog). Ladders not passable for dogs are on ‘adventure’ section of trail. Quiet as soon as you get off the main lookout trail but busy before then. Lots of nice lookouts.
Fantastic hike!! Highly recommend!
Beautiful trail ADVENTURE TRAIL IS A MUST DO!!! Cave exploring through amazing time!

Excellent intermediate trail, well marked and maintained. The "Adventure Trail" was worth the effort but it can be challenging. You can follow the yellow trail or follow the blue marked side trails but only if you like EXTRA challenging. Traffic was medium to heavy on the red trail and completely tranquil on the blue longer loop. Beautiful views whichever loop you choose.
Great hike! Went on a Thursday morning around 8:30/9 and didn’t see anyone until the last km coming back. Lots of scenic views, trail is fairly well marked. Just pay attention to your all trails
we took the blue trail and it a small section isnt marked but if you follow the well packed trail there is no issue.
Tough with kids to complete
Hard to find the blue trail near the east lookout
Awesome. but they don't spend alot of money on markers!

Did the red and blue loops on a Monday morning and had the trail to myself except for the last ten minutes on the way back to the parking lot. Did the blue loop clockwise and did have to pull out AllTrails a couple of times to make sure I was on the right trail. Don’t skip the blue loop! Tons of scenic vistas that aren’t shown on the map.
Red trail of cup snd saucer well marked, nice views at top. Blue trail not well marked, many more outcropping views rampant poison ivy.

Great! Good to have back up map as there are parts of the trail not labelled great most are. Good to go in morning by the time we left the parking lot was very full. Recommend doing the blue loop if you have time!
Great trail, nice and dry, no bugs today but terribly marked!
Good trail! well signed! make sure if you do the loop to not follow the quad trail!
we went left on the loop because of the steep incline so on the way back it wasn't as steep on the way down. if you prefer a slower start and a steep ending then go right at the loop.
Beautiful trail.

Beautiful views on the island. We went in late April (off season) and there was only one other person on the trail! It was a tiny bit muddy since we had a rainy day a few days before we hiked this, but easy enough to navigate through it. Rocky and moderately challenging!
Great trail
My boyfriend and I hiked the trail today it was a moderate trail! The lookouts and the views were beautiful! Loved it!
awesome
Lovely trail with a few challenging sections. Definitely need proper  footwear. Recommend  doing the loop because  of the many vistas.

Chiefs kiss! Loved it. Took me just over 3 hours. Did the loop counter clockwise and I'm glad I did. At 2:30pm the lot was packed but by the time I got up there I had the place to myself. I tried to do the "adventure trail" going down but my (70lb) dog wouldn't have managed the wood ladder section, glad I didn't try to take it up or I would have had to turn around. I did this hike in (sports) sandals because of reviews saying not to. I had no problems but I also hike it them a lot. As long as you have good tread on wet rock, your feet don't slide around in them, and you're used to doing similar km have at her.
Awesome
Easy to navigate trail, pretty views, but if elevation but nothing too crazy. Wear proper footwear.

This was a very fun hike! We chose to do both the “adventure trail” (yellow) and the longer blue trail. The adventure trail had lots of caves to explore and rocks to climb, definitely recommend tackling that part! The blue trail included plenty of scenic views and beautiful forestry, however there is one particular stretch of the trail that is poorly marked, though the path itself is quite obvious. Concluding thoughts: be ready for a long day, bring some snacks, and charge up your camera!

well maintained. Not sure why other comments said not well marked...markers were everywhere. 
Recommend doing the entire loop, beautiful hike. 

Wear proper footwear, and get there early. 
we saw no one at 8:30, and on our way down we
Nice hike. It was a little easier than I expected from previous comments, but agree that sturdy footwear is a must. Make sure to do it counter-clockwise as the trail and views get better as you go!

The trail has two parts to it that make for a good half day hike.  The first portion is about 5km and offers a good blend of ambling over rock and flat trails sections that are under a canopy of trees.  Be. Mindful on the stair section and be patient with those going up or down.  There are three lookout points along the way,  do them all!  The views are worth it.
The second section of the trail is much less technical and can seem a bit bland in comparison to the first section.  Watch our for downed trees and roots on the descent.  Bring water and snacks and sturdy shoes.  This is not a flip-flop sandal trail.
Nice lookouts and a well maintained trail
big rock shape like tea cup me like

Arrive early or late day to avoid crowds.  The main viewpoint and trail were empty when I hiked around 7 a.m., but the trail was packed passing people on the way back and the parking lot was crammed.  A really nice trail with several great view points.  you can extend it doing the adventure loop and connecting the red and blue trails, which is about 9 km.  the adventure is the one section I'd describe as being slightly higher than moderate.  the rest is fairly easy with proper footwear.  it seems like it could have a lot of wet areas depending on rain.
Excellent trail! Go early for less crowds during peak season.
beautiful views

This popular Manitoulin Island hike had a great effort for reward ratio, as the short trail and reasonably quick ascent led to a wonderful view. 

I would highly recommend the longer Blue Trail loop after the ascent to escape the crowds and experience multiple vantage points to yourself. 

Also notable was the traffic.  We arrived at the trailhead for 800a and were the 3rd car there.  But by 1130a the parking lot was nearly at capacity with 70 cars or trucks.  Come early to avoid the crowds.
Great trail! Some more challenging sections and some easier sections. Very busy on the red trail. Blue part of trail was very quiet

great spot. adventure trail was well worth it. we started with the larger blue loop and ended at the adventure trail which was a better way to do it I think. only be noce if there were either more maps located through the trail or better markings.

Great hike! Views were beautiful and the hike was just the right amount of challenging. I agree that the hike is moderate but some people may find some sections hard (big steps/climbing/steep slopes). Keep an eye out for side trails as they can be easy to miss if you're not paying attention.

Great trail. Adventure trail really gets ur heart racing a bit. We didn’t do the blue extension because we were too scared of how close it gets to the edge of the cliff. Everything is well marked, quite busy but not horrible. Free parking, ports potties. Definitely a must do hike!
Good climbing on the first 2.5 K to a bunch of lookouts, then a nice 6 km through the forest around back￼￼
Definitely an adventure!
The majority of people skip the blue loop and they are truly missing out!

Porta potty at site, no payment for parking.  enjoyed the trail took us 5 hrs cause we lolly gagged around, got lost once but found our way back. not busy at alllllll at 9am but once we left at 3pm was packed parking lot. was a great view and adventure trail was fun . no bugs swarming very enjoyable.
Great trail. Like the other reviews, download the maps so you don't get too lost plus to make sure you hit the adventure trail.

Only one on the trail on a Monday morning. Great views Manitoulin and the forest and good signage for the various look outs. I did the Adventure Trail on the way up, which is a mix of rock scramble, makeshift ladders, and steeper trail. For a fit hiker, I'd grade this as easy with some moderate bits. Some bugs in the lookout areas.
One of my favorites.  Hiking over tons of rock and amazing views.  I did the 5k walk with my 6 year old and gf.  Trail could be marked a little better as some markers fell of the trees.
One of my favourite trails in Ontario. Beautiful views and great walk through woods.

Great trail with lots of beautiful views. The trail markers have been torn off in some areas so definitely happy we had the all trails map to guide us. It was rainy today and so was a bit muddy and slippery, but otherwise excellent.
Beautiful loop! It’s not really difficult. Wouldn’t rate it moderate, but there is a bit of rocks and ‘climbing’ involved.
Great trail. 2nd time completing, this time doing the full loop instead of just the lookout. Fall colours make for amazing scenic sights.
The red trail can be rigorous but enjoyable with the blue trail providing many lookouts perfect for a lunch stop. Great hike with nice views.
Easy and well maintained

Probably the best trails I have ever done. The adventure trail is alot of fun albeit can be very difficult. I would recommend going with a buddy and hiking shoes/boots are a must. If you want to stop and have lunch, enjoy the views and do the adventure trail I would set aside 4 hours or so. There are some parts on the blue trail that are not always labelled very well so be careful, we would have gotten lost if it wasn't for my Garmin watch.

Great hike! I did the adventure trail as well. Although I wish the adventure trail was marked a little better, as long as you follow the cliff edge you won’t get off trail. If you do the adventure trail, make sure to follow the ‘Lookout’ signs to get back. It’s a little confusing when you come back to the main trail. 

Amazing views of Manitoulin Lake and surrounding area. 

The blue trail is an easy 5km hike through a forest.

Hiked the red and blue trail.  It is worth doing the blue trail as it continues along the escarpment edge for more great views without the crowds.  A few steep but short sections at the beginning of the trail but I would class this as easy not moderate.  
Trail was in good condition - dry - well signed.  The whole trail was 14km if you start on the red trail and continue to do the blue loop.  It took us about 4 hours.
Great trail, well maintained, my wife and I  did all the trails, definitely do the adventure trails some nice climbing spots and inukshuks. Beautiful view all the way around from the top.
Awesome!!
Great views. Trails not very well marked in some areas

Did the red to blue loop clockwise. The escarpment was beautiful and lots of lookouts. Red route was busy, I didn’t see another soul on the blue route. 

I thought I heard some black bears nearby on the blue part, and then lost the trail when I hit what looked like an access road. Thankfully the all trails GPS got me back to the route, but if I hadn’t had signal I would have been screwed. Good reminder to bring map and compass. 

After our bushwhacking adventure my dog got too tired and I had to heave him over logs, and I really didn’t think he was going to make it down the last set of stairs. 

Giving it a lower score for poor signage in spots and no warning about the bears. I read afterwards thats Manitoulin has the highest bear density in Ontario.
some nice outlook points. possiable to walk even in the rain, not that muddy. after the outlook not crowded.

The trail is in good condition and pretty popular. We went on a weekday and the parking was full by the time we left at 3:00 ish, though the parking lot is big! The blazes are clear. If you just want to go see the view points, take the main trail (red blazes) loop, keeping to your left at the fork. We did the side loop (blue blazes) anticlockwise, which means we hiked through the wood before going up to the escapement. It took us about 2.5 hours b4 hitting the high points but we liked it. There are various rock platforms along the cliffs, which are good spots for views and photos! The biggest extension is at the end, a good spot to rest and take in the scenery. Beware of the strong wind if you want to stand close to the edge! When we headed back, we took the adventure trail (yellow blazes). It’s not too difficult but you’re gonna climb a bit and walk on wooden staircases. The adventure trail is a small detour route (500 m) of the main trail, as it merges to it on both ends. However, I think doing it anticlockwise (on your return) is easier as you would be descending rather than going uphill. Overall, the trail is rocky and full of tree roots. Sturdy footwear is recommended. To make the main loop and the blue loop, plus a lunch break and several photo stops takes about 3.5-4 hours.

Do the adventure trail! Stones, sketchy ladders, and other awesome things. Definitely easier to get lost there, but the alltrails map will take you back. Spectacular set of lookouts at the top. The trail is as beautiful as the rest of the island :)

The trail is in good condition and pretty popular. We went on a weekday and the parking was full by the time we left at 3:00 ish, though the parking lot is big! The blazes are clear. If you just want to go see the view points, take the main trail (red blazes) loop, keeping to your left at the fork. We did the side loop (blue blazes) anticlockwise, which means we hiked through the wood before going up to the escapement. It took us about 2.5 hours b4 hitting the high points but we liked it. There are various rock platforms along the cliffs, which are good spots for views and photos! The biggest extension is at the end, a good spot to rest and take in the scenery. Beware of the strong wind if you want to stand close to the edge! When we headed back, we took the adventure trail (yellow blazes). It’s not too difficult but you’re gonna climb a bit and walk on wooden staircases. The adventure trail is a small detour route (500 m) of the main trail, as it merges to it on both ends. However, I think doing it anticlockwise (on your return) is easier as you would be descending rather than going uphill. Overall, the trail is rocky and full of tree roots. Sturdy footwear is recommended. To make the main loop and the blue loop, plus a lunch break and several photo stops takes about 3.5-4 hours.
Best to be prepared. Lots of climbing and uneven ground. Amazing views are the payoff.
Great trail. Some parts may be difficult for young children or people with physical difficulties, but overall the trail is clear of debris and not very muddy. Recommended to anyone in area.

Overall great trail. Early parts of the trail easy to moderate, lots of tourists. Beautiful lookouts, take the adventure trail   . Rest of the trail is pretty easy. walk it backwards if you want to see the lookouts early. Great trail for dogs as well.

This is a BUSY trail. You know it's a tourist destination when hikers passing you by are wearing cologne and perfume LOL  I encountered dozens of people and the sound of transports could be heard for much of the trail. Most of this trail is easy and all age groups were walking the trail. The adventure trail was a fun part of the hike and the lookouts are beautiful. Be sure to stop at Whitefish Falls on your way to the trail! If you paddleboard, the river is quiet and lovely.
Great views!

Shaded in the woods. The first bit had no bugs (without bug spray!). There are some high stairs and a bit of a climb when you follow the main trail, but once you're up you get a nice view. Would suggest to do this early - when I returned there were a lot of people starting the hike (I started at 8/830 ish). Trail is friendly for big dogs - if you have a small or medium sized dog you may have to help them climb up and down the stairs (the only way for the main trail).
Awesome.

Amazing trail, mostly kid friendly, just make sure to keep them close at the lookouts and some spots along the (blue) loop trail.  The adventure section (yellow) was amazing, some parts were a challenge with a 4 and 8 year old on a rainy day, but worth it in the end.  the shorter red trail offers a walk through an amazing forest with a few fun climbs, and the loop is a peaceful trek through the woods with lots of cool plants and mushrooms for the kids to check out.  Took us 4 and a half hours with 2 kids, lots of stops to see things, and the added time on the challenging adventure course.
Let me tell you, this was THE BEST hike I’ve ever done. If you take the adventure trail, there are dark caves to walk through and loads of fun photo shoot places. SO WORTH IT!
great trail. we did the full 10km loop which took us just under 3 hours with a lunch stop along the way. lost a star due to quarry noise and trash along the trail. great views.

Very fun and beautiful trail. We did the red and yellow parts and it made for a great morning!
The yellow was a bit more challenging but very fun with ladders and rock scrambles to try! The red is quite direct to the scenic lookouts and the views are incredible.

Great trail! Stayed mostly on the red trail. Attempted to do some of the blue trail but the friend I was with has vertigo and spots in the blue trail were a little to on the edge of her. The views were amazing. It was starting to get busy - mostly families with kids - when we left. Would recommend going earlier in the day if you can.
Nice views! Full trail took us about 3 hours. A few rocky parts.
moderate trail with awesome Lookouts

We started on the the Red Trail, picked up the Blue Loop, and then rejoined the Red.  My GPS clocked us at 8.6km.    The Red Trail was slightly more challenging than the Blue.  You'll want sturdy shoes.  I use walking poles, and was glad to have them, but they aren't necessary.  Along the Red Trail there are signs for "The Lookout" which we didn't check out.  There are several lookout spots along the Blue so we felt we didn't need another spot.  There are a few points, along the Blue,  where the markings switch to white.  Don't worry... you are still on the Blue.  The mornings are quieter... go early.

I was waiting for the 3 oclock ferry in South Baymouth, having lunch when AllTrails brought me to this trail... i jumped in the car  took the 40 min drive, ran up to the lookouts... then ran down (only wiping out once... slippery little roots) and made the 40 min drive back with 12 mins to spare. The view was worth it 100% next time I will allow my self more time to enjoy it!
Good trail conditions and great views.
Great trail and views - highly recommend
great trail, the adventure trail is adventurous to say the least.

We loved the 10km loop! We got there early to avoid running into many hikers. We had our puppy with us and he loved it as well. Took about 4 hours, made many stops for pictures and ate a full lunch at the top. Could do it in 3 hours if you didn’t stop as much. Recommend! 5/5

This is a lovely trail! It’s a bit busy near the beginning with families with young children but as you go further into the trail it gets a lot calmer. It’s a beautiful simple trail with some amazing lookouts. It took us about 2.5 hours with some stops so it’s quite easy. Would entirely recommend this for a nice half day trip.
Good views, good workout
very well signed, and very beautiful

Great trail & great views!!
Take water if you’re hiking in the summer, the trail is a great workout if you complete it in an hour & 45 like I did

Nice trail. I recommend the adventure trail, yellow trail on the map, for those who want a bit more challenge. It's not hard if your used to hiking and some bolder climbing. The main trail goes to the same lookout but I find it more boring. I did the blue loop. You have a few more lookout on the blue trail but after the first few ones the rest have very similar view. The rest of the blue trail is mostly flat forest trail. I would pass the blue loop not missing much. Maybe go to the first few lookout on the blue trail and go back.
Did the adventurous part, the best part of the trail! Took about 3 hours to do the red, adventure and blue sections.
It was a very nice day. We took the blue trail that leads into the red into the yellow.

Some great views here and a good trail length for a quick morning or afternoon hike.  Most sections are easy, but there are a couple places where you have to scramble a bit and/or climb a sketchy looking ladder.
